Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=4x & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=4 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi x) & ⇒ & v=-\frac{1}{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi x).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 4x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi x)\,\text{d}x & =4x\cdot (-\frac{1}{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi x))-\int (-\frac{1}{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi x))\cdot 4\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}4x\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi x)\,\text{d}x & =-\frac{4}{\pi }x\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi x)\,{|}_{0}^{1}+\frac{4}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{1}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{4}{\pi }x\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi x)\,{|}_{0}^{1}+\frac{4}{{\pi }^{2}}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi x)\,{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =-\frac{4}{\pi }(1\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi \cdot 1)-0\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi \cdot 0))+\frac{4}{{\pi }^{2}}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi \cdot 1)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi \cdot 0)) \\  & =-\frac{4}{\pi }(-1-0)+\frac{4}{{\pi }^{2}}(0-0) \\  & =\frac{4}{\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$
